model: M6 play outcome model, call view (gradient-boosted trees)

settings.protocol: M6 protocol: the 4-setting grid is fit on 2016..S-2 and scored on S-1 (CRPS); the winner is refit on 2016..S-1 with its early-stopped tree count. The same fitted model drives the 2026 fourth-down engine.

license.credit: Data: nflverse (CC BY 4.0); participation data from NFL Next Gen Stats via nflverse (2016-2022) and FTN Data via nflverse (2023+). Numbers on this page derive from participation data and are released under CC BY-SA 4.0.

headline.window: 2020-2025, season-ahead, REG + POST (locked holdout, scored once)
headline.plain: On the locked 2020-2025 seasons the model's yard distributions beat the historical down-distance-field baseline in every season and both data eras; the gain is small because most of a play's outcome is not predictable before the snap.

bins.note: bin 0 = 10+ yards lost, bins 1-50 = -9..+40 yards, bin 51 = 41+ yards short of the end zone, bin 52 = touchdown (reported as p_td, not in `bins`). Bins that are impossible from the yard line are folded (gains past the goal line become touchdowns).

held_neutral.team_ratings: league average (0) for the offense's pass/rush and the defense's pass/rush ratings
held_neutral.home: averaged: half the draws home, half away
held_neutral.structure: defensive personnel, formation and box count are not fixed: each cell averages the model over 32 draws of (defensive personnel, formation, box) from 2016-2025 plays with the same offensive personnel and call in the most specific matching situation with at least 200 plays (down x distance bucket x field zone, else down x distance, else distance, else all); `structure_pool` is that pool's size

fields.exp_yards: expected yards (descriptive; 10+ lost counted as -12, 41+ as 55, a TD as the yard line)
fields.p_first_or_td: P(gain reaches the line to gain, or a touchdown)
fields.p_turnover: P(interception or lost fumble), separate model
fields.n_similar: 2016-2025 plays with the same down, distance, call and personnel within 5 yards of the yard line: thin support means read the cell with care

caveats: A prediction for the snap, not a promise: most of a play's outcome cannot be known before it.
Held-neutral inputs: real games differ (score, clock, weather, the two teams).
Cells with small n_similar (rare situations, e.g. 1st and 3 outside goal-to-go) rest on the model's smoothing more than on direct data.
Run versus pass here is the called play type; it is not a recommendation (see the play-calling page).
